## DEV-01. For January 5–30, 2026, how many therapy sessions did Rowan attend, by service type and in total, and on how many distinct days? Provide a reviewable abstraction with source support and explain records that could lead to duplicate or ineligible counts.

- Rowan attended 12 therapy sessions (individual, group, and family psychotherapy) between January 5–30, 2026, across 11 distinct days: 5 individual sessions (January 5, 14, 19, 21, 26), 5 group sessions (January 6, 12, 19, 22, 29), and 2 family sessions (January 9, 30). Including the 2 medication management visits also attended in the period, the total of all attended visits is 14 across 12 distinct days. — HG-E104: [family_primary_jan09.txt:4-10](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L4-10), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:13](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L13); - Several records require attention to avoid duplicate or ineligible counts: (1) The appointment desk export lists 9 encounters in one document — each is a separate visit counted once, not an additional session. (2) The outpatient attendance and disposition register lists 4 encounters (January 22, 27, 28, 29) in one document; each is counted once. (3) For the January 19 group session (HG-E110), four documents exist: the original roster, a copy retransmitted January 26 (no new information, not counted separately), a correction filed January 20 updating Rowan's departure time, and the group clinical record — all refer to the same single session. (4) The January 9 family session (HG-E104) has a co-facilitator addendum and a scheduling support log entry (a planned record, not an actual visit); both support the one counted session. (5) The scheduling support log also records an undated outbound phone call with no answer — no encounter number, not a therapy session, not counted. (6) A billing/administrative chart extract exists for the January 27 group no-show (HG-E116); that visit was not attended and is not counted, but the charge document could suggest a session occurred if reviewed in isolation. (7) January 19 has two counted therapy sessions — a group (HG-E110) and an individual (HG-E111) added because Rowan became anxious during group and needed individual grounding; both are legitimate distinct encounters. (8) January 30 has two attended visits — a family therapy session (HG-E119, counted) and a medication management visit (HG-E120, not counted as therapy). (9) The January 26 individual session (HG-E115) is documented by two clinicians whose notes give different start times (09:00 vs. 09:10) and different durations (50 vs. 40 minutes); attendance is agreed, so the session counts once, but the duration remains unresolved. — HG-E110: [BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt#L1-6), [BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt#L1-6), [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:1-5](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L1-5); ## DEV-05. Summarize the documented symptom course during the episode and the reason for the additional individual contact on January 19. Which symptom assessments are distinct, and what conclusions about progress can and cannot be supported?

- At intake (January 5), Rowan presented with several weeks of low mood, reduced interest in activities, fragmented sleep with repeated night waking, difficulty beginning tasks, and work-related anxiety driving avoidance of emails and conversations about a return date. Through the first two weeks these symptoms persisted largely unchanged: sleep remained interrupted, mornings were difficult, and avoidance of work communication continued, though Rowan noted mood felt somewhat less heavy on days with a planned activity (January 13). By mid-episode (January 14–16) the clinician observed affect more varied than at intake, and a clinician review noted some improvement in depressive symptoms while avoidance and inconsistent sleep continued. On January 19 Rowan became visibly tense and overwhelmed during group discussion of workplace demands. In the final week, Rowan sent a message to the supervisor (January 26) but continued to postpone scheduling the follow-up conversation; sleep remained uneven, tied to repetitive work-related thoughts at night. By January 30 Rowan reported mood felt less persistently low than earlier in the month, though anxiety about work contact remained noticeable and sleep was still variable. — finding: [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:10](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L10), [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:4-8](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L4-8); ## DEV-07. The January 12 roster says Rowan attended the full group. How much patient therapy time should be credited, and why?

- Rowan should be credited with 75 minutes of patient therapy time for January 12. — HG-E105: [early_group_attendance_roster.txt:11](../documents/early_group_attendance_roster.txt#L11), [early_group_attendance_roster.txt:11](../documents/early_group_attendance_roster.txt#L11), [group_facilitator_jan12.txt:12](../documents/group_facilitator_jan12.txt#L12)
- That figure is calculated from a documented arrival of 10:00 and departure of 11:30 (a 90-minute window), minus a 15-minute group break from 10:40 to 10:55, leaving 75 creditable minutes. The session ran as scheduled. — HG-E105: [early_group_attendance_roster.txt:11](../documents/early_group_attendance_roster.txt#L11), [group_facilitator_jan12.txt:12](../documents/group_facilitator_jan12.txt#L12), [group_facilitator_jan12.txt:12](../documents/group_facilitator_jan12.txt#L12), [group_facilitator_jan12.txt:4-8](../documents/group_facilitator_jan12.txt#L4-8), [group_facilitator_jan12.txt:4-8](../documents/group_facilitator_jan12.txt#L4-8), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:14](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L14)
- Three independent sources — the appointment desk export, the group facilitator's clinical note (Leena Park, LPC), and the group desk attendance roster — all confirm Rowan attended the full session. The desk note further records that Rowan checked in before the group began and remained until the group was released. The facilitator's note documents active participation throughout. ## DEV-08. Which January 19 group departure time should be used after considering all versions of the attendance record, and what makes that version authoritative for this field?

- The departure time to use for the January 19 group session is 11:15. This comes from the attendance correction document signed by Leah Chen, LCSW on January 20, 2026, which supersedes the original roster's entry of 11:30. — HG-E110: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:7](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L7), [BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt:8-10](../documents/BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt#L8-10); passage: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:9](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L9), [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:11](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L11)
- The correction is authoritative for this field because it is a signed, clinician-authored correction (not a copy or retransmission) that explicitly identifies the original error — the original roster had inadvertently carried forward the scheduled group closing time of 11:30 into Rowan's departure field — and replaces it with 11:15, confirmed against the room-transfer record showing Rowan leaving skills room B and being received by the individual clinician at 11:15. The record applies the rule that a signed correction supersedes the original for the field it corrects. *(inference)* — HG-E110: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:7](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L7), [BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt:8-10](../documents/BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt#L8-10); finding: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:9](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:11](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L11); passage: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:9](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L9), [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:11](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L11)
- The resent roster received on January 26 (a copy, not a new clinician-signed document) still shows 11:30, but it carries no independent authority: it is a retransmission of the original pre-correction roster and adds no new clinician signature, so it does not override the correction. — passage: [BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt:10-16](../documents/BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt#L10-16); HG-E110: [BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt#L1-6), [BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt#L1-6), [BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt:10-16](../documents/BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt#L10-16)

## DEV-09. The January 21 video export contains two call IDs. How many therapy sessions should an encounter-level abstraction contain, and how much contact time?

- The January 21 encounter-level abstraction should contain 1 therapy session. The video export's two call IDs (VC-112A and VC-112B) represent the same appointment split by a network disconnect — the second call was a rejoin of the original — and the record treats them as a single attended individual psychotherapy encounter. — HG-E112: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:3](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L3), [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:5](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L5), [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:7](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L7); passage: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:17](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L17), [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:18](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L18), [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:19-20](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L19-20)
- The abstraction should record 45 minutes of contact time. This is the sum of the two call segments (13:00–13:20 and 13:30–13:55), with the 10-minute gap between them (13:20–13:30) excluded as a break, yielding 20 + 25 = 45 minutes — confirmed by the note's stated total of 45 minutes of patient psychotherapy contact. — HG-E112: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:7](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L7), [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:7](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L7), [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:7](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L7), [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:17](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L17); passage: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:17](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L17), [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:18](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L18)

## DEV-10. Calculate Rowan’s eligible group minutes on January 22. Does participation after the break establish attendance at the beginning of the group?

- Rowan's eligible group minutes on January 22 are 45. The session ran 10:00–11:30 with a nontherapeutic break from 10:45–11:00. Rowan arrived at 10:30 and stayed until the group closed at 11:30, giving 60 minutes of presence, minus the 15-minute break, for 45 creditable minutes. — HG-E113: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:9](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L9), [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:9](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L9), [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:7-10](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L7-10); passage: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:9](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L9), [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:7-10](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L7-10)
- Participation after the break does not establish that Rowan was present at the beginning of the group. The record documents a late arrival at 10:30 — 30 minutes after the 10:00 start — and the clinical note explicitly states that Rowan joined the discussion after it had begun. The note of Rowan contributing an example after the break reflects participation during the second half of the session, not the opening. — HG-E113: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:9](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:7-10](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L7-10); finding: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:7-10](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L7-10); passage: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:9](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L9), [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:7-10](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L7-10)

## DEV-11. How many therapy minutes should be assigned to the January 29 group, and which records are needed to establish them?

- The January 29 group session should be assigned 75 creditable therapy minutes. ## DEV-12. How much of the January 30 family appointment contributes to Rowan’s treatment-plan minute goal? Explain the difference from the therapist’s session duration.

- 30 minutes from the January 30 family appointment count toward Rowan's treatment-plan patient-present therapy minute goal. The goal credits only the time Rowan was present in the session. — HG-E119: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7); G:patient-present therapy minutes: [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:12](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L12); passage: [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:12](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L12)
- The 15-minute difference arises because Rowan did not join until 13:15; the first segment (13:00–13:15) was partner-only time. The treatment-plan goal counts only patient-present minutes, so that opening segment is excluded, leaving 30 of the 45 therapist minutes creditable to Rowan. *(inference)* — HG-E119: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7); passage: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:12](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L12)
- The therapist's documented session duration is 45 minutes (13:00–13:45), covering the full interval from when the session began with Casey Mercer alone through its end. — HG-E119: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7); passage: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7)

## DEV-16. What happened to the January 8 individual appointment and follow-up call, and how should each affect therapy counts and minutes?

- The January 8 individual therapy appointment (scheduled 11:00–11:45) was a no-show: Rowan did not arrive by the close of the appointment slot, reception notified the clinician that no check-in or cancellation had been received, and the appointment was marked no-show. It is excluded from therapy counts and contributes no minutes toward any goal. — HG-E103: [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:11](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L11), [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:11](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L11), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:12](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L12), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:20](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L20), [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:4-7](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L4-7), [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:4-7](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L4-7); finding: [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:9](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L9)
- Following the no-show, an outbound call was placed to the patient's recorded number; there was no answer and a brief callback request was left without clinical detail. The call addressed scheduling and contact information only — no therapy intervention was conducted — and the individual clinician was notified so that barriers to attendance could be discussed at the next visit. The call is not recorded as a therapy encounter and does not count toward session totals or minutes. — passage: [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:13](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L13), [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:17](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L17); finding: [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:17](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L17); finding: [early_appointment_status_export.txt:20](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L20)
- Because Rowan did not attend the January 8 individual appointment, it is excluded from the week of January 5–11. That week's goal-eligible therapy count remains 3 sessions (January 5, 6, and 9) totaling 140 minutes — meeting the 3-day threshold but not the 150-minute threshold. *(inference)* — HG-E103: [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:11](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L11), [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:11](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L11), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:12](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L12); HG-E101: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:4-9](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L4-9), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:10](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L10); HG-E102: [group_facilitator_jan06.txt:14](../documents/group_facilitator_jan06.txt#L14), [group_facilitator_jan06.txt:14](../documents/group_facilitator_jan06.txt#L14); HG-E104: [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:7-9](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L7-9), [family_primary_jan09.txt:4-10](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L4-10), [missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt:15](../documents/missed_visit_outreach_jan08.txt#L15)

## DEV-17. Why was the January 15 group not delivered, and is it accurate to describe this as a patient no-show or a refusal of therapy?

- The January 15 coping skills group was not delivered because the clinic cancelled it due to staff illness, with no covering facilitator available. The group was removed from the active room schedule, a portal notice was sent to participants before the 10:00 start time instructing them not to come, and no group was held and no participants were seen. — HG-E108: [early_appointment_status_export.txt:20](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L20), [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:9](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L9), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:17](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L17); finding: [early_appointment_status_export.txt:20](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L20); finding: [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:9](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L9); finding: [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:11](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L11); finding: [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:15](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L15); passage: [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:11](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L11), [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:15](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L15)
- It is not accurate to describe this as a patient no-show. The appointment was cancelled by the clinic, not missed by the patient. Participants were proactively notified before the scheduled start time and told not to attend; the non-delivery was entirely on the clinic's side. *(inference)* — HG-E108: [early_appointment_status_export.txt:17](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L17), [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:9](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L9), [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:15](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L15); finding: [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:9](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L9); finding: [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:11](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L11); passage: [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:11](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L11)
- It is not accurate to describe this as a patient refusal of therapy. The record contains no documentation of the patient declining or refusing to attend. The cancellation was initiated by the office due to staff illness, and participants were instructed by the clinic not to come. — HG-E108: [early_appointment_status_export.txt:20](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L20), [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:9](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L9); finding: [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:11](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L11); passage: [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:11](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L11)

## DEV-20. How should the January 23 care-coordination call be represented when counting Rowan’s therapy, and did it change treatment frequency or medication?

- The January 23 care-coordination call is excluded from therapy counts and does not count toward any therapy day or minute goal. Rowan did not participate — the call was between the clinician (Mira Patel, LCSW) and an outside social worker only, with no patient contact. The treatment plan explicitly states that care coordination does not contribute to the therapy day or minute goals. — HG-E114: [BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt:1-7](../documents/BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt#L1-7), [BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt:1-7](../documents/BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt#L1-7), [BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt:1-7](../documents/BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt#L1-7), [BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt:13](../documents/BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt#L13); passage: [BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt:1-7](../documents/BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt#L1-7), [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:12](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L12)

## DEV-32. A summary assigns 55 minutes to the January 21 video visit because it spans 13:00–13:55. Is that abstraction supported? Provide the corrected calculation.

The record documents a 10-minute connection loss from 13:20–13:30 during which there was no therapeutic contact; that interval must be subtracted from the 13:00–13:55 span. — HG-E112: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:7](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L7), [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:17](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L17); passage: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:7](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L7)

## DEV-33. Across the January 9 family visit, January 16 collateral contact, and January 30 family visit, how much documented clinician session time involved family or partner work, and how much qualifies as Rowan’s patient-present family therapy?

- Across the three contacts, total documented clinician session time was 130 minutes: 45 minutes on January 9 (family visit, Rowan and Casey both present the full session), 40 minutes on January 16 (collateral contact with Casey only), and 45 minutes on January 30 (family visit, therapist interval 13:00–13:45). — HG-E104: [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:6](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L6), [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:6](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L6), [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:6](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L6); HG-E109: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:6](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L6), [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:6](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L6), [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:6](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L6); HG-E119: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7)
- Of that 130 minutes, 75 minutes qualify as Rowan's patient-present family therapy: the full 45 minutes on January 9 (Rowan and Casey were both present for the entire session) and 30 minutes on January 30 (Rowan joined at 13:15 and participated through 13:45; the first 15 minutes were partner-only). The January 16 collateral contact contributes none, because Rowan did not join in person, by telephone, or by video, and no patient-present psychotherapy occurred during that contact. — HG-E104: [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:6](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L6), [family_primary_jan09.txt:4-10](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L4-10), [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:6](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L6), [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:7-9](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L7-9); HG-E119: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7); finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:17](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L17); passage: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7), [family_primary_jan09.txt:4-10](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L4-10), [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:7-9](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L7-9); HG-E109: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:4](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L4), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:18](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L18), [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:7-9](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L7-9)

## DEV-39. What are the absolute and percentage changes in PHQ-9 from intake to the final assessment? Show the denominator and avoid inferring functional recovery from the calculation.

- The PHQ-9 dropped by 8 points from intake (January 5, 2026) to the final assessment (January 30, 2026): from 18 to 10. The denominator for the percentage calculation is the intake score of 18. — M:PHQ-9 2026-01-05: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:15](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L15), [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-30: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L1-6); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-16: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:4-9](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L4-9)
- The percentage change is −44.4%, calculated as the 8-point drop divided by the intake score of 18. This is a symptom score change only; the record does not support drawing conclusions about functional recovery from this calculation alone. — M:PHQ-9 2026-01-05: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:15](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L15), [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-30: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L1-6)
- The January 16 PHQ-9 score of 14 (form HG-Q116) appears in the record through a document described as an administrative import receipt — a copy received January 26, not an original clinical submission. It is also supported by a separate symptom measure review note from January 16. Because the January 16 score is the middle assessment and neither the intake nor the final score, the copy status of that import document does not affect the intake-to-final change calculation; the intake score of 18 (January 5) and the final score of 10 (January 30) each come from independent sources unrelated to that import. — M:PHQ-9 2026-01-16: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:4-9](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L4-9); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-05: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:15](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L15), [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-30: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L1-6); passage: [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:13](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L13)

## DEV-42. By January 30, what evidence supports improvement and what evidence limits a conclusion of recovery? Integrate symptoms with functioning.

- Evidence supporting improvement: The PHQ-9 fell from 18 on January 5 to 14 on January 16 and to 10 on January 30, a trajectory the clinician described as partial improvement. Rowan's own report on January 30 was that mood felt less persistently low than earlier in the month, with fewer days of pervasive low mood than at intake. Functionally, Rowan completed small activities by January 14 (opening a work message, short walks), and by January 26 had sent a message to the supervisor and received a reply — a concrete step not present at intake. Affect was noted to be more varied than at intake by January 14. Casey confirmed Rowan was getting out for walks and seemed more willing to discuss the coming week by January 16, and the scheduled evening check-in had reduced unplanned reminders. On January 30 Rowan was alert, organized in conversation, and able to describe the follow-up plan, and reported that having a limited plan felt more manageable. — finding: [BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt:8](../documents/BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt#L8); finding: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:8](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L8); finding: [individual_therapy_jan14.txt:11](../documents/individual_therapy_jan14.txt#L11); finding: [individual_therapy_jan14.txt:15](../documents/individual_therapy_jan14.txt#L15); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:9](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L9); finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:13](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L13); finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:13](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L13); finding: [BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt:10](../documents/BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt#L10); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:13](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L13); passage: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:10](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L10); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-05: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:15](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L15), [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-16: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:4-9](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L4-9); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-30: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L1-6)
- Evidence limiting a conclusion of recovery: Despite the PHQ-9 decline, a score of 10 on January 30 remains in the mild-to-moderate range, and the clinician explicitly characterized the picture as partial improvement with persistent avoidance and meaningful functional impact around returning to work. Avoidance of work communication was unresolved throughout: Rowan had not replied to the original work message as of January 14, drafted but did not send a message until around January 26, and as of January 29–30 was still delaying the follow-up conversation with the supervisor after receiving a reply. Sleep disruption persisted across every week of the period — described as interrupted, inconsistent, or variable on January 5, 13, 14, 16, 21, 26, and 30 — and the clinician noted it remained an intermittent barrier to a steadier daytime routine. Anxiety remained noticeable when anticipating work contact on January 30 (patient and clinician reports), and Rowan became visibly tense during group discussion of workplace return on January 19, requiring a same-day individual session. The pattern of reminders triggering withdrawal was still active on January 30, and Rowan continued to delay scheduling the supervisor conversation even after the message was sent. — finding: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:10](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L10); ## DEV-43. Trace Rowan’s work-communication progress from early January through January 30. Distinguish a planned action, drafting, sending, and completed follow-up.

- Planned actions: From January 5, the treatment plan set out that individual sessions would address avoided communication and gradual preparation for return to employment, and that the team would combine individual, group, and family work. Rowan expressed wanting a manageable work-transition routine. On January 9, Casey agreed to a single planned check-in about work preparation rather than repeated reminders. On January 13, Rowan was directed to bring activity and communication concerns to the treating therapist. On January 19, the plan after the individual crisis visit was to review how the smaller task went at the next visit. On January 23, the outside social worker was to provide contact information and help organize documents if requested. On January 26, the plan included maintaining scheduled treatment contact during the return-to-work period and bringing the response draft to the next visit if Rowan remained stuck. On January 30, the plan was to continue the current outpatient treatment and revisit whether the agreed communication pattern had been useful. — finding: [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:18](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L18); finding: [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:10](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L10); finding: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:11](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L11); finding: [family_primary_jan09.txt:16](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L16); finding: [medication_review_jan13.txt:17](../documents/medication_review_jan13.txt#L17); finding: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:13](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L13); finding: [BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt:11](../documents/BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:13](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L13); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:13](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L13)
- Drafting activity: On January 14, a session focused on separating a brief acknowledgment from a commitment to a work schedule; a short response was drafted in Rowan's own words and practiced aloud. On January 19, the task was narrowed to drafting two sentences to a supervisor without requiring the message be sent that day, and Rowan was encouraged to allow an incomplete draft to exist rather than abandon it over imperfect wording. By January 21, Rowan reported having drafted a short message about a possible gradual return to work but stopping before sending it; the session then practiced reading the draft once and choosing a planned time to send it. Rowan also identified repeatedly checking the draft as a further way of delaying the task. — finding: [individual_therapy_jan14.txt:13](../documents/individual_therapy_jan14.txt#L13); finding: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:11](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:9](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:9](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:9](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L9)
- Sending activity: By January 26, Rowan reported having sent a short message to the supervisor and receiving a reply asking to discuss possible next steps. The January 26 session rehearsed a brief response to that reply, with Rowan's partner Nora Ellis helping rehearse a grounding cue to use before sending it. The record does not document whether that follow-on response was actually sent after the session. — finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:9](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:11](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:11](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L11); passage: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:9](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L9)
- Completed follow-up: On January 14, Rowan reported completing several small activities since the prior individual appointment, including opening a work message. The supervisor's reply to Rowan's sent message (received before January 26) constitutes the one documented external response: it reduced one uncertainty but raised worry about being asked for commitments Rowan might not be able to meet. By January 29, Rowan reported opening the work calendar but delaying the follow-up conversation with the supervisor. The January 30 clinician review noted that Rowan had taken initial steps including drafting and sending a message, but continued to delay follow-up and became anxious when a task expanded beyond a narrowly defined action. — finding: [individual_therapy_jan14.txt:11](../documents/individual_therapy_jan14.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:9](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:12-15](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L12-15); passage: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:10](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L10)

## DEV-44. What prompted the additional individual therapy contact on January 19, what was done, and what immediate response was documented?

- The visit was added because Rowan became anxious during the group session — specifically, when group discussion turned to returning to the workplace, Rowan became visibly tense, said the amount of discussion felt difficult to manage, and requested additional help. The group facilitator arranged a same-day individual meeting with the treating clinician, and Rowan came directly from the group room. — finding: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:9](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt:10](../documents/BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt#L10), [BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt:14](../documents/BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt#L14); finding: [BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt:14](../documents/BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt#L14); finding: [BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt:10](../documents/BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt#L10), [BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt:14](../documents/BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt#L14)
- During the 30-minute individual session, the clinician used paced breathing, orientation to the room, and a brief review of Rowan's coping card. The work-related task was then narrowed to drafting just two sentences to a supervisor — without requiring the message be sent that day — and the clinician discussed allowing an incomplete draft to exist rather than abandoning the task over imperfect wording. The plan was to continue the established outpatient plan and review how the smaller task went at the next individual visit. — finding: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:11](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:11](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:13](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L13); HG-E111: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:1-7](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L1-7)
- Rowan reported that the immediate intensity of anxiety eased enough to discuss a next step. No acute safety concern was identified; Rowan denied suicidal thoughts and remained future-oriented in discussing the next appointment. — finding: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:11](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:13](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L13)

## DEV-45. Identify the recurring psychotherapy strategies used for avoidance and task initiation, with examples from different dates. What evidence distinguishes rehearsal from independent follow-through?

- Two recurring strategies address avoidance: (1) psychoeducation about the anxiety–avoidance cycle — mapping the sequence from triggering situation → anxious prediction → physical activation → avoidance response (January 5, developing a shared description of the sleep/worry/avoidance cycle; January 19 group, worked example using an unanswered work email); and (2) behavioral activation / approach behavior selection — identifying and committing to a small, observable approach step rather than withdrawing (January 5, breaking one work task into a short observable step; January 19 group, members selected a small approach behavior to attempt during the week; January 22 group, translating a broad intention into one action completable in a few minutes). — finding: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:17](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L17); finding: [BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt:8](../documents/BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt#L8); finding: [BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt:8](../documents/BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt#L8); finding: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:7-10](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L7-10)
- Two recurring strategies address task initiation: (1) task decomposition — breaking a complicated task into the smallest observable first step and identifying the cue that would prompt it (January 5, practicing breaking one work task into a short observable step; January 14, narrowing the work task to drafting two sentences without requiring the message be sent; January 19 individual, narrowing to drafting two sentences and allowing an incomplete draft to exist; January 22 group, reducing a task to an action completable in a few minutes with a named cue; January 23 coordination review, helping Rowan break a difficult task into a manageable first step); and (2) in-session rehearsal of the specific action — practicing the wording, timing, or communication step aloud before attempting it independently (January 6, practicing breaking a task into a step; January 14, drafting a short response in Rowan's own words and practicing it aloud; January 21, practicing reading the draft once and choosing a planned send time; January 26, role-play of a brief response to the supervisor; January 26, rehearsing requesting a brief initial conversation with a specific purpose; January 30, rehearsing requesting a specific kind of help from Casey). — finding: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:17](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L17); finding: [individual_therapy_jan14.txt:13](../documents/individual_therapy_jan14.txt#L13); finding: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:11](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:7-10](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L7-10); finding: [group_facilitator_jan06.txt:10](../documents/group_facilitator_jan06.txt#L10); finding: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:9](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:11](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt:10](../documents/BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt#L10); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:11](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt:11](../documents/BH-D109_care_coordination_2026-01-23.txt#L11)
- The clearest distinction between rehearsal and independent follow-through is documented on January 26: Rowan could use the grounding cue during the in-session rehearsal but remained uncertain about using it independently when anxious, and the clinician noted the patient was hesitant about completing the task outside the office. This directly contrasts structured, clinician-supported practice (rehearsal) with self-initiated use under real anxiety (independent follow-through). The pattern across the record reinforces this: rehearsal produced engagement and partial skill use with prompting, while between-session reports consistently showed partial completion — approach steps started but not carried through to the next stage. — finding: [BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt:12](../documents/BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt#L12); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:13](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L13); finding: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:9](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:12-15](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L12-15); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:9](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L9); passage: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:10](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L10)
- Rehearsal is documented as clinician-facilitated, in-session practice: January 6, the facilitator demonstrated paced breathing and invited short practice rounds; January 9, Rowan practiced asking for one specific kind of help while Casey practiced reflecting the request, with a communication rehearsal guided by the clinician; January 14, a short response was drafted and practiced aloud in session; January 21, Rowan practiced reading the draft once and choosing a planned send time; January 26, clinicians used role-play to identify when Rowan shifted from asking a question into apologizing, and a grounding cue was rehearsed before sending; January 29, Rowan participated in a paired rehearsal and accepted feedback about keeping the request brief; January 30, a rehearsal was facilitated in which Casey asked what kind of support Rowan wanted and Rowan practiced naming when a reminder felt overwhelming. — finding: [group_facilitator_jan06.txt:10](../documents/group_facilitator_jan06.txt#L10), [group_facilitator_jan06.txt:4-8](../documents/group_facilitator_jan06.txt#L4-8); finding: [family_primary_jan09.txt:14](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L14); finding: [family_primary_jan09.txt:14](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L14); finding: [individual_therapy_jan14.txt:13](../documents/individual_therapy_jan14.txt#L13); finding: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:9](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:11](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:11](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:11](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:12-15](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L12-15)
- Independent follow-through — applying skills between sessions without clinician support — is documented through patient self-report at subsequent visits: January 9, Rowan said an evening walk felt more acceptable than reviewing unfinished tasks (approach behavior attempted outside session); January 21, Rowan reported having drafted a short message about a gradual return to work but stopping before sending it; January 26, Rowan reported sending the message to the supervisor and receiving a reply, but continued to postpone choosing a time for the follow-up conversation; January 29, Rowan reported opening the work calendar but delaying a follow-up conversation. A January 30 clinician review noted that Rowan had taken some initial steps including drafting and sending a message, but continued to delay follow-up. — finding: [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:15](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L15); finding: [BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt:9](../documents/BH-D106_telehealth_2026-01-21.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:9](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:9](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:12-15](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L12-15); passage: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:10](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L10)

## DEV-46. Summarize the course of sleep difficulty during the episode. Does the record support saying that sleep normalized by the final week?

- Sleep difficulty was present throughout the episode and never fully resolved. At intake (January 5), Rowan described several weeks of fragmented sleep, and the clinician listed sleep disruption as a presenting need. On January 8, a poor night of sleep caused Rowan to miss an appointment. Sleep interruption and daytime tiredness continued through January 13–14. By January 16, the clinician noted some improvement in depressive symptoms but described sleep as still inconsistent and clinically relevant. On January 19, disrupted sleep continued to interfere with resuming a work routine. On January 21, Rowan reported one improved night followed by a night of prolonged wakefulness. On January 26, sleep remained uneven, tied to repetitive work-related thoughts at night. At the episode's close on January 30, Rowan still endorsed sleep difficulty, described sleep as variable, and the clinician noted sleep disruption as an intermittent barrier to a steadier daytime routine. — finding: [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:10](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L10), [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:4-8](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L4-8); - The record does not support saying sleep normalized by the final week. In the last week (January 26–30), both the patient and the clinician consistently described sleep as uneven, variable, and an ongoing barrier. The plan on January 30 was to continue monitoring sleep, not to note resolution. The only positive change noted by episode end was fewer days of pervasive low mood, not improvement in sleep. — finding: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:9](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt:8](../documents/BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt#L8); finding: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:8](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L8); finding: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:10](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L10); finding: [BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt:10](../documents/BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt#L10); passage: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:8](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L8)

## DEV-47. Which January 16 observations came from Casey, and which came from Rowan’s own questionnaire update? Why does that distinction matter?

- Casey's observations came from the collateral contact (encounter HG-E109), a session with Mara Voss, LCSW and Casey Mercer alone — Rowan was not present. Casey reported four things: that Rowan had been getting out for short walks and seemed more willing to discuss the coming week; that mornings remain difficult and Rowan becomes quiet when conversation turns to work; that the scheduled evening check-in has reduced unplanned reminders; and that it takes effort to resist offering multiple solutions, but there is less argument when Casey asks what kind of help Rowan wants. — finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:13](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L13), [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:6](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L6); finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:13](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L13), [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:6](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L6); finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:13](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L13), [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:6](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L6); finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:13](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L13), [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:6](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L6); HG-E109: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:7-9](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L7-9), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:20](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L20)
- Rowan's own questionnaire update — a PHQ-9 submitted through the patient portal on January 16 at 08:17, with an optional free-text field — contributed three findings in Rowan's own words: getting out of the apartment had become a little easier; thinking about work continued to make them want to put things off; and sleep was inconsistent. — finding: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11); finding: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11); finding: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-16: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:4-9](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L4-9); passage: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11)
- The distinction matters because the two sources carry different clinical weight. Casey's account reflects an outside observer's perspective on Rowan's behavior at home — useful for tracking functioning but filtered through Casey's interpretation. Rowan's own questionnaire responses reflect Rowan's subjective experience directly. Where they overlap (e.g., both sources note sleep difficulty and avoidance of work topics), the agreement strengthens confidence in those findings. Where they differ in emphasis — Casey noted improved willingness to discuss the coming week, while Rowan's own words focused on ongoing avoidance — the clinician noted that Casey's information would be incorporated only at the next direct appointment with Rowan, and that no treatment decision was made on the basis of the collateral contact alone. *(inference)* — finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:13](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L13); finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:13](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L13); finding: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11); finding: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11); finding: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:17](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L17); passage: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:11](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L11)

## DEV-48. What family communication plan was developed on January 9, and how was that theme revisited on January 30? Does the later note prove the issue was already resolved?

- On January 9, the family session (with Rowan, Casey, Mara Voss LCSW, and Leena Park LPC) produced a three-part communication plan: (1) Casey agreed to replace repeated reminders with a single planned check-in about work preparation; (2) Rowan agreed to say when they wanted practical help versus quiet company; and (3) the couple chose a shared evening walk as a pressure-free activity. Clinicians used reflective listening exercises and a communication rehearsal to help both partners understand how their intentions differed from how the other experienced them. — finding: [family_primary_jan09.txt:16](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L16); finding: [family_primary_jan09.txt:16](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L16); finding: [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:15](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L15); finding: [family_primary_jan09.txt:14](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L14); finding: [family_primary_jan09.txt:14](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L14); finding: [family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt:13](../documents/family_cofacilitator_jan09.txt#L13); finding: [family_primary_jan09.txt:12](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L12); finding: [family_primary_jan09.txt:18](../documents/family_primary_jan09.txt#L18)
- On January 30, the family session (encounter HG-E119, with Mira Patel LCSW) revisited the same theme: Rowan and Casey identified that the pattern of reminders about contacting work was still leading to lengthy discussions followed by Rowan withdrawing from the task, and Casey still described uncertainty about when reminders helped versus increased pressure. The clinician ran another communication rehearsal — Casey practiced asking what kind of support Rowan wanted, and Rowan practiced naming when a reminder felt overwhelming. Both then agreed again to try one brief, planned check-in rather than repeated questions across the evening. The plan noted that whether the agreed communication pattern had been useful would need to be revisited at a future visit. — finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:11](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L11), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:1-3](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L1-3); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:9](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L9), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:1-3](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L1-3); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:11](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L11), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:1-3](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L1-3); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:13](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L13), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:1-3](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L1-3); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:13](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L13), [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:1-3](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L1-3); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:1-3](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L1-3); passage: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:13](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L13)
- The January 30 note does not prove the issue was already resolved. On the contrary, it documents the same recurring pattern still present — reminders continuing to trigger withdrawal — and the plan explicitly defers judgment on whether the agreed communication approach was working. Rowan remained anxious about the work conversation, and the clinician's overall assessment was partial improvement with persistent avoidance and meaningful functional impact. *(inference)* — finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:11](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L11); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:9](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:13](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L13); finding: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:13](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L13); finding: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:10](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L10)

## DEV-52. Which formal psychiatric diagnosis and diagnostic code are established by these documents? Distinguish clinical symptom descriptions from a coded diagnosis.

- No formal coded psychiatric diagnosis (such as an ICD-10 or DSM-5 code) is recorded anywhere in these documents. The record does not contain a diagnosis field, a diagnostic code, or a named disorder assigned by a clinician. *(not documented)*
- The closest the documents come to a diagnostic impression is the clinician's characterization at intake: "depressive symptoms with anxiety and behavioral avoidance." A later assessment entry reads "ongoing depressive and anxiety symptoms with sleep disruption." These are clinical impression statements, not a coded diagnosis. A formal diagnosis with an ICD or DSM code, entered in a diagnosis field and signed by a treating clinician, would be needed to establish a coded disorder. — finding: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:15](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L15); finding: [medication_review_jan13.txt:15](../documents/medication_review_jan13.txt#L15)
- The clinical symptom descriptions documented across the record, distinct from any coded diagnosis, include: low mood and reduced interest in usual activities for several weeks; fragmented and interrupted sleep with daytime fatigue; difficulty beginning ordinary tasks; worry and anxiety about returning to work; avoidance of work communication (delaying email replies, not sending drafted messages, postponing scheduling a conversation with a supervisor); behavioral avoidance that worsens with discussion of workplace demands; muscle tension, rapid breathing, and an urge to leave as physical signs of anxiety; repetitive planning at night interfering with sleep; ## DEV-57. What reasons are documented for Rowan’s partial group attendance on January 6 and late arrival on January 22? Can the same explanation be assigned to both dates?

- On January 6, the record documents two reasons for partial attendance: Rowan arrived late after difficulty finding parking (calling from the building entrance to say they were running behind), and left early for a previously arranged ride. — HG-E102: [early_group_attendance_roster.txt:13](../documents/early_group_attendance_roster.txt#L13); finding: [early_group_attendance_roster.txt:13](../documents/early_group_attendance_roster.txt#L13); finding: [early_group_attendance_roster.txt:13](../documents/early_group_attendance_roster.txt#L13)
- On January 22, the record documents only "late arrival" as the reason for partial attendance. Rowan arrived at 10:30 and remained until the group closed at 11:30; no reason for the late arrival is recorded. — HG-E113: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:9](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:14](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L14); passage: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:9](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L9)
- The same explanation cannot be assigned to both dates. On January 6, parking difficulty is explicitly documented as the cause of late arrival, and an early departure for a pre-arranged ride also contributed to the partial attendance. On January 22, no cause for the late arrival is recorded — the record notes only that Rowan joined after the group had begun. A note documenting the reason for the January 22 late arrival would be needed to determine whether the circumstances were the same. *(inference)* — HG-E102: [early_group_attendance_roster.txt:13](../documents/early_group_attendance_roster.txt#L13); finding: [early_group_attendance_roster.txt:13](../documents/early_group_attendance_roster.txt#L13); HG-E113: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:9](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L9); finding: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:7-10](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L7-10); passage: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:9](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L9)

## DEV-58. Give three examples in which a signature, receipt, or import date differs from the underlying service or assessment date. Explain the effect on date-based counts.

- Three examples where a document date differs from the underlying service or assessment date: (1) The PHQ-9 scored on January 16, 2026 was imported and filed on January 26, 2026 — ten days after the patient completed the questionnaire. (2) The group attendance roster for the January 19 skills group (HG-E110) was resent and received on January 26, 2026; intake staff indexed the copy under the service date printed on the roster (January 19), but the receipt date is the inbox processing date of January 26. (3) The attendance correction for HG-E110 was entered on January 20, 2026, the day after the January 19 service date, to fix Rowan's departure time from 11:30 to 11:15. — passage: [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:4-8](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L4-8), [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:17](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L17), [BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt:8](../documents/BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt#L8), [BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt:10-16](../documents/BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt#L10-16); HG-E110: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:7](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L7), [BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt:8-10](../documents/BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt#L8-10); finding: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:9](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L9)
- The effect on date-based counts depends on which date is used. If a system counts measurements or visits by the date a document was received or filed rather than the date of the underlying service, the PHQ-9 completed January 16 would appear in a January 26 count instead of a January 16 count, and the resent roster for the January 19 group would similarly shift to January 26. Using the receipt date of the correction (January 20) rather than the service date (January 19) for HG-E110 could cause that visit to be counted in a different day or week. Anchoring counts to the service or assessment date — as the record does — prevents these shifts. *(inference)* — passage: [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:4-8](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L4-8), [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:17](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L17), [BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt:8](../documents/BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt#L8); HG-E110: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:7](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L7), [BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt:8-10](../documents/BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt#L8-10)
- The Harbor Grove Behavioral Health administrative import receipt for the PHQ-9 dated January 16, 2026 is a copy filed on January 26, 2026 at 07:44. It records a score of 14 with an original completion date of January 16 (form identifier HG-Q116). The import operator was N. Ellis. The receipt itself does not document a new patient visit; it copied the result from the January 16 portal form into the chart. No newly completed questionnaire was included in the batch. The measurement tab retains the original patient submission, and the assessment date for this PHQ-9 remains January 16, 2026 — not January 26. — passage: [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:4-8](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L4-8), [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:13](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L13), [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:17](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L17), [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:19](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L19); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-30: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L1-6); M:PHQ-9 item 9 2026-01-30: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L1-6); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-16: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:4-9](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L4-9); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-05: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:15](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L15), [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11)

## DEV-59. A reviewer resolves all discrepancies by selecting the latest received or latest signed document. Would that rule produce defensible answers for January 19 and January 26?

- For January 19, the rule produces a defensible result. There are no unresolved conflicts on that date: all facts are corroborated, established, or documented. The one document that arrived latest — the re-sent roster received January 26 — is a copy with no new clinician signature and records no additional visit, so selecting it over the earlier originals changes nothing of substance. The departure-time discrepancy was already resolved by a formal correction signed January 20, which the record accepted; the rule would reach the same answer. *(inference)* — HG-E110: [BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt:7](../documents/BH-D103_attendance_correction_2026-01-20.txt#L7), [BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt:8-10](../documents/BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt#L8-10), [BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D101_group_content_2026-01-19.txt#L1-6), [BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D102_original_attendance_2026-01-19.txt#L1-6), [BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt:10-16](../documents/BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt#L10-16); passage: [BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt:20](../documents/BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt#L20), [BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D104_resent_roster_received_2026-01-26.txt#L1-6); HG-E111: [BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt:1-7](../documents/BH-D105_individual_2026-01-19.txt#L1-7)
- For January 26, the rule does not produce a defensible result. The two individual psychotherapy records for that visit are both final, actual clinical documents — one signed by Mira Patel, LCSW at 11:16 and one signed by Nora Ellis, LCSW at 12:03. Selecting the later-signed document (Nora Ellis's) would resolve the start-time conflict (09:00 vs. 09:10) and the duration conflict (50 vs. 40 minutes) in favor of 40 minutes, but that document records the shorter time precisely because it uses the later start time. The two records are of equal standing and neither corrects the other; the conflict is substantive, not a clerical error, and a mechanical tie-breaking rule cannot determine which start time is clinically accurate. *(inference)* — HG-E115: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:5-7](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L5-7), [BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt:10](../documents/BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt#L10), [BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt:6-8](../documents/BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt#L6-8); passage: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:15-16](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L15-16), [BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt:16-17](../documents/BH-D111_individual_second_record_2026-01-26.txt#L16-17)

## DEV-60. Can the final Monday–Sunday week be reported as a complete observed week through February 1? Explain the review-period boundary and the strongest supported weekly conclusion.

- No, the final Monday–Sunday week cannot be reported as a complete observed week through February 1. The review period ends on January 30, 2026, which is a Friday — not a Sunday — so it does not fall on a Monday–Sunday week boundary. The final week (January 26–February 1) is only observed through January 30; January 31 and February 1 fall outside the authorized episode and have no recorded encounters, so extending the week to February 1 would add two days with no data rather than resolve the partial-week status. — G:therapy days: [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:4-8](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L4-8); G:patient-present therapy minutes: [signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt:4-8](../documents/signed_treatment_plan_jan05.txt#L4-8); G:group sessions: [group_authorization_letter.txt:9-10](../documents/group_authorization_letter.txt#L9-10); HG-E115: [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:5-7](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L5-7), [BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt:5-7](../documents/BH-D110_individual_primary_record_2026-01-26.txt#L5-7); HG-E118: [BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt:12-15](../documents/BH-D107_group_activity_records_2026-01-22_and_29.txt#L12-15), [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:20](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L20); HG-E119: [BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt:6-7](../documents/BH-D113_family_therapy_2026-01-30.txt#L6-7); HG-E116: [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:16](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L16), [BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt:16](../documents/BH-D108_final_attendance_and_cancellation_register.txt#L16); HG-E120: [BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt:5](../documents/BH-D114_medication_management_2026-01-30.txt#L5)

## DEV-61. Which record pairs or groups should be linked as documentation of the same underlying event rather than counted as separate events? Include both encounters and symptom measurements.

- One encounter pair should be linked: the unnumbered family contact on January 16 mentioned in the group cancellation notice (BH-D016) and the collateral encounter HG-E109 on the same date. Both share the same date, service type (family/collateral), and issuing source. The January 16 reference is not a separate event — it is a forward reference to the appointment that was already documented and counted as HG-E109. No other encounter pairs or groups in the review period require linking; all remaining encounters are distinct events with different dates, service types, or clinicians. — HG-E109: [partner_collateral_jan16.txt:4](../documents/partner_collateral_jan16.txt#L4), [early_appointment_status_export.txt:18](../documents/early_appointment_status_export.txt#L18); unnumbered family contact on 2026-01-16 (group_cancellation_notice_jan15): [group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt:13](../documents/group_cancellation_notice_jan15.txt#L13)
- For PHQ-9 measurements: the January 30 total score (10) and the January 30 item 9 score (0) are parts of the same assessment event — both completed at 12:42 on January 30 from the same document — and should be read together as one administration, not counted as two separate assessments. The January 5 (score 18) and January 16 (score 14) PHQ-9 records are each distinct assessment events on different dates and should remain separate from each other and from the January 30 assessment. — M:PHQ-9 2026-01-30: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L1-6); M:PHQ-9 item 9 2026-01-30: [BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt:1-6](../documents/BH-D115_symptom_measure_review_2026-01-30.txt#L1-6); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-16: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:4-9](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L4-9); M:PHQ-9 2026-01-05: [intake_and_individual_jan05.txt:15](../documents/intake_and_individual_jan05.txt#L15), [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:11](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L11)
- The Harbor Grove Behavioral Health administrative import receipt received January 26 is a copy — an administrative summary imported from the patient portal — not an independent administration of the PHQ-9. It lists the January 16 PHQ-9 (score 14, form HG-Q116) and corroborates that assessment, but adds no independent evidentiary weight to it. The January 16 score therefore rests on a single independent source (the symptom measure review note, BH-D013), with the import receipt serving only as a copy. The January 16 PHQ-9 remains one documented assessment event and is not duplicated by the import receipt. — M:PHQ-9 2026-01-16: [symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt:4-9](../documents/symptom_measure_review_jan16.txt#L4-9); passage: [imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt:13](../documents/imported_measure_summary_received_jan26.txt#L13)

## DEV-62. Would the appointment-status export alone support an accurate therapy-minute total for January 5–16? Identify what additional evidence is necessary.

- The appointment-status export alone is not sufficient to produce an accurate therapy-minute total for January 5–16.
